feedback.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=3{x}^{2}+2$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=3{x}^{2}+2$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(3{x}^{2}+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[{x}^{3}+2x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }({\pi }^{3}+2\pi )-0 \\  & =2({\pi }^{2}+2).\end{aligned}
$$
